definition: willing to listen to or accept new ideas and suggestions

The young queen proved more receptive to reform than her father had been.
My coach was surprisingly receptive when I suggested a new warm-up.

questions.passage: The engineers expected the board to reject their proposal. To their surprise the directors were ______, asking detailed questions and agreeing within the hour to fund a pilot project.
questions.explanation: Asking questions and agreeing to fund shows willingness to accept the idea.

distractors.why: Incoherent means unclear and confused, which does not fit.
Inconspicuous means not easily noticed, which does not fit.
Forthright means direct and honest, which is not the contrast with rejecting.

The summer reading list encompasses everything from comics to Shakespeare.

confused.note: To encompass is to include or surround; a compass shows direction.

questions.passage: The park is far larger than most visitors realize. It ______ not only the famous canyon but also two mountain ranges, a desert, and more than a thousand kilometers of river.
questions.explanation: Containing a canyon, ranges, a desert, and rivers is including a wide range.

distractors.why: Relinquishes means gives up, which does not fit.

Good pizza transcends all disagreements in my family.

confused.note: To transcend is to rise beyond limits; to descend is to go down.

questions.passage: The best children's books ______ the age of their intended readers. A story written for seven-year-olds may be read with equal pleasure, and for different reasons, by their parents and grandparents.

distractors.why: Forgo means to do without, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin scandere, "to climb": to climb across

My notes from the 8 a.m. lecture are incoherent.

confused.note: Incoherent means unclear or illogical; inherent means built in.

questions.passage: The first draft of the report was nearly ______. Paragraphs contradicted one another, tables had no labels, and the conclusion referred to findings that appeared nowhere in the text.

distractors.why: Sophisticated means highly developed, the opposite of this muddle.

questions.passage: The suspect claimed that he had found the stolen painting lying in a field. Detectives considered the story ______, since the canvas was spotless and it had rained heavily all week.

distractors.why: Receptive means open to ideas, which does not describe a story.

Perpetual means never ending, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin plaudere, "to applaud": not worth applauding

questions.passage: Detectives were ______ for months. Every lead ended at the same locked warehouse, whose owner could not be found and whose records had been destroyed in a fire.

distractors.why: Fortified means strengthened, which does not fit.

questions.passage: The entrance to the famous restaurant is deliberately ______. There is no sign, the door is painted the same gray as the wall, and first-time visitors often walk past it twice.
questions.explanation: An unmarked gray door that visitors walk past is hard to notice.

distractors.why: Sophisticated means refined or complex, which does not fit.
Perpetual means never ending, which does not fit.

My little cousin has a surprisingly sophisticated taste in cheese.

confused.note: Sophisticated means advanced or worldly; sophomoric means immature and overconfident.

questions.passage: The ancient device, recovered from a shipwreck, is far more ______ than anyone expected. Its thirty interlocking bronze gears could predict eclipses and track the positions of five planets.
questions.explanation: Thirty gears that predict eclipses are highly developed and complex.

distractors.why: Incoherent means confused, which does not fit.
Implausible means hard to believe; the device exists and works.

Whether cilantro tastes good is entirely subjective.

questions.passage: Judging a diving competition is partly ______. Two experts watching the same dive may award different scores, since each weighs grace, height, and the smoothness of the entry in her own way.

distractors.why: Perpetual means never ending, which does not fit.
Intangible means unable to be touched, which is not the point.
Ample means plentiful, which does not fit.

partsNote: thrown under, dependent on the self

There was ample time to finish the test, but I still rushed.

confused.note: Ample means plentiful; to amble is to walk slowly.

questions.passage: The defense could not claim that it had been surprised. The court had given both sides ______ notice, announcing the date of the trial eight months in advance.
questions.explanation: Eight months is more than enough notice.

distractors.why: Intangible means unable to be touched, which does not fit.
Implausible means hard to believe, which does not fit.
Inconspicuous means hard to notice, the opposite of well-announced notice.

The narrator lives in perpetual fear of being found out.
My little brother is in a state of perpetual motion.

confused.note: Perpetual means never stopping; perennial means lasting or recurring year after year.

questions.passage: Near the poles in midsummer, the sun never sets. Travelers who arrive from farther south often find it hard to sleep in the ______ daylight and cover their windows with blankets.
questions.explanation: Daylight that never ends continues without stopping.

distractors.why: Implausible means hard to believe, which does not fit.
Subjective means based on opinion, which does not fit.
Receptive means open to ideas, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin petere, "to seek": seeking throughout

definition: to copy or repeat something exactly

The colony tried to replicate the laws of the mother country.
I have never managed to replicate my grandmother's gravy.

questions.passage: A finding is not accepted merely because one team reports it. Other scientists must be able to ______ the experiment, following the same steps and arriving at the same result.

distractors.why: Relinquish means to give up, which does not fit.
Aggravate means to make worse, which does not fit.
Satirize means to mock through humor, which does not fit.

definition: not able to be touched; hard to describe or measure exactly

examples.text: Morale is intangible, but its effect on a crew's performance is real.
The victory brought intangible gains in prestige.
The old gym had an intangible quality the new one lacks.

confused.note: Intangible means unable to be touched or measured; intractable means hard to manage.

questions.passage: The company's most valuable assets are ______. Its factories and trucks are worth far less than its reputation, its customers' loyalty, and the knowledge of its engineers.
questions.explanation: Reputation, loyalty, and knowledge cannot be touched.

distractors.why: Ample means plentiful, which is not the contrast with factories and trucks.
Perpetual means never ending, which does not fit.
Incoherent means unclear, which does not fit.

definition: to make something louder, stronger, or greater

The empty stairwell amplified every footstep.

confused.note: To amplify is to increase; amply means more than sufficiently.

questions.passage: The canyon's shape ______ sound. A person speaking in a normal voice at one end can be heard clearly by someone standing nearly a kilometer away at the other.

distractors.why: Stymies means blocks, the opposite of carrying sound farther.

partsNote: from Latin amplus, "large": to make large

definition: to give up something, such as power, a claim, or a possession

My brother finally relinquished the remote after three hours.

confused.note: To relinquish is to give up; to replenish is to refill.

questions.passage: The founder had run the company for fifty years and could not imagine life without it. Only when her eyesight failed did she agree to ______ control to her daughter.
questions.explanation: Handing control to her daughter is giving it up.

distractors.why: Amplify means to increase, the opposite of giving up control.
Replicate means to copy, which does not fit.
Reprimand means to scold officially, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin linquere, "to leave": to leave behind

definition: to decide not to have or do something that you would like

examples.text: The general chose to forgo an easy victory and let the enemy retreat.
Patients must forgo food for twelve hours before the test.
I will forgo dessert tonight, since I ate it before dinner.

confused.note: Forgo means to do without; "forego" strictly means to go before, though it is often used for both.

questions.passage: To save money for the expedition, the students agreed to ______ their usual summer holiday. They spent July and August working in a cannery and put every paycheck toward the cost of the boat.
questions.explanation: Giving up their holiday is choosing to do without it.

distractors.why: Fortify means to strengthen, which does not fit.
Satirize means to mock, which does not fit.
Amplify means to increase, which does not fit.

examples.text: The governor fortified the harbor with a chain of stone towers.
The cereal is fortified with iron and vitamin D.
I fortified myself with a large breakfast before the hike.

confused.note: To fortify is to strengthen; fortune is luck or wealth.

questions.passage: Fearing an invasion from the sea, the city spent ten years ______ its coast. Engineers built a wall eight meters high along the beach and placed cannon on every headland.
questions.explanation: Building a wall and placing cannon strengthens the coast against attack.

distractors.why: Relinquishing means giving up, the opposite of defending.
Rebutting means arguing against, which does not fit.
Replicating means copying, which does not fit.

examples.text: The admiral was reprimanded for sailing without orders.
The headmaster reprimands the boy in front of the whole school.
The referee reprimanded both captains before the second half.

confused.note: To reprimand is to scold officially; to remand is to send back, as to custody.

questions.passage: The hospital did not dismiss the nurse. It did, however, formally ______ her, placing a letter in her file that described the error and warned that a second would cost her the job.
questions.explanation: A formal letter describing the error is an official scolding.

distractors.why: Fortify means to strengthen, which does not fit.
Transcend means to go beyond, which does not fit.
Encompass means to include, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin premere, "to press": to press back

confused.note: To aggravate is to make worse; an aggregate is a total.

questions.passage: The doctor warned the runner not to return to training too soon. Even a short jog, she said, could ______ the injury and turn a three-week recovery into three months.
questions.explanation: Making a three-week injury last three months is making it worse.

distractors.why: Relinquish means to give up, which does not fit.
Replicate means to copy, which does not fit.
Fortify means to strengthen, the opposite of worsening an injury.

partsNote: from Latin gravis, "heavy": to make heavier

confused.note: Forthright means frank and direct; forthcoming means about to appear, or willing to share information.

questions.passage: Most officials answered the committee's questions with vague phrases. The engineer was more ______: she said plainly that the bridge was unsafe, that she had warned her superiors, and that they had ignored her.
questions.explanation: Saying plainly what happened is direct and honest.

distractors.why: Receptive means open to ideas, which is not the contrast with vague answers.
Inconspicuous means hard to notice, which does not fit.
Subjective means based on opinion, which does not fit.

questions.passage: Each side in the debate was given ten minutes to state its case. The teams were then allowed five minutes apiece to ______ the arguments their opponents had made.

distractors.why: Replicate means to copy, which is the opposite of arguing against.

questions.passage: For years the small bookshop resisted offers from the chain that had bought every other store on the street. In the end it ______, and the last independent shop in the district closed its doors.

distractors.why: Transcended means rose above, the opposite of giving in.
Rebutted means argued against, which does not fit.
Amplified means increased, which does not fit.

questions.passage: To explain why the stars at the edge of the galaxy move so quickly, astronomers ______ the existence of matter that cannot be seen. No one has yet detected it directly.

questions.passage: The composer wrote more than two hundred works. All of them have been ______ by a single short piano piece, which is played so often that most listeners assume he wrote nothing else.

questions.passage: For three days the river covered the lower streets of the town. When the waters finally ______, residents returned to find mud a meter deep in their kitchens.

questions.passage: With its glass towers, crowded trains, and shops that never close, the district ______ the modern city. Filmmakers who need a single image of urban life almost always shoot it there.

distractors.why: Overshadows means makes seem less important, which does not fit.

My notes are a haphazard pile of sticky notes and napkins.

questions.passage: The library's collection had grown in a ______ manner. Books were shelved wherever space happened to be free, and a visitor looking for a history of France might find it between a cookbook and an atlas of the moon.

questions.passage: Long before it was popular, the senator ______ the cause of clean rivers. She introduced the first bill on the subject in 1961 and reintroduced it in every session for twelve years until it passed.

She harbors a grudge against the cousin who inherited the house.
I harbor a secret hope that the test will be postponed.

confused.note: To harbor is to shelter or hold a feeling; an arbor is a shaded garden structure.

questions.passage: Though she smiled and shook his hand, the losing candidate continued to ______ doubts about the result. For years afterward she told friends that the count in three districts had never been properly explained.
questions.explanation: Keeping doubts for years is holding them in mind.

distractors.why: Capitalize means to take advantage, which does not fit.
Epitomize means to exemplify, which does not fit.
Correlate means to relate two things, which does not fit.

definition: to allow or accept something you do not like; to bear

examples.text: The plant can tolerate drought but not frost.
The king tolerated criticism from poets but not from priests.
I tolerate my brother's music because he tolerates my singing.

confused.note: Tolerate is the verb; tolerant is the adjective.

questions.passage: The new manager made it clear that she would not ______ lateness. Anyone arriving after nine without a good reason, she announced, would lose an hour's pay.
questions.explanation: Punishing lateness shows she will not accept it.

distractors.why: Champion means to support actively, the opposite of refusing to accept.
Embody means to give form to, which does not fit.
Recede means to move back, which does not fit.

definition: to suggest something without saying it directly

examples.text: Her silence implies more than any reply could.
The data imply that the lake was once much larger.
Are you implying that I ate the last cookie?

confused.note: A speaker implies; a listener infers.

questions.passage: The letter never says that the factory will close. It does, however, ______ as much, advising workers to "consider their options" and to "prepare for significant changes in the coming months."
questions.explanation: Advising workers to prepare suggests closure without stating it.

distractors.why: Infer means to draw a conclusion; the letter suggests, and readers infer.
Tolerate means to put up with, which does not fit.
Overshadow means to make seem less important, which does not fit.

definition: serious and sincere

examples.text: The earnest young clerk believes every word of the company's motto.
The envoy made an earnest plea for peace.
My little cousin gave an earnest speech about why we should adopt a goat.

confused.note: Earnest means sincere; earnings are money earned.

questions.passage: The student's essay was not polished, but it was ______. She wrote with obvious feeling about her grandmother's illness and made no attempt to impress the reader with long words.
questions.explanation: Writing with real feeling and no showing off is sincere.

distractors.why: Lax means careless, which is not what the description praises.
Disinterested means impartial, which does not describe heartfelt writing.
Provisional means temporary, which does not fit.

definition: arranged for the present time only and likely to be changed

examples.text: A provisional government ruled until elections could be held.
The species was given a provisional name until its relatives were identified.
My schedule is provisional until the coach posts practice times.

confused.note: Provisional means temporary; provincial means narrow or regional.

questions.passage: The committee stressed that the timetable was ______. It would be revised once the engineers had inspected the tunnel and could say how long repairs would take.
questions.explanation: A timetable that will be revised is arranged for now and likely to change.

distractors.why: Definitive means final, the opposite of a timetable awaiting revision.
Rigid means fixed and unbending, which a revisable timetable is not.
Earnest means sincere, which does not fit.

partsNote: seen to for the time being

definition: reminding you of someone or something

examples.text: The novel's opening is reminiscent of a fairy tale.
The new palace was reminiscent of the Roman villas its owner admired.
The smell of the bakery is reminiscent of my grandmother's kitchen.

confused.note: Reminiscent is the adjective; a reminiscence is a memory that is told.

questions.passage: The young painter's use of light is ______ of the Dutch masters. Like them, she places her figures beside a single window and lets the rest of the room fall into shadow.
questions.explanation: Her technique brings the Dutch masters to mind.

distractors.why: Disinterested means impartial, and it does not fit "of the Dutch masters."
Scarce means in short supply, which does not fit.
Preliminary means coming first, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin mens, "mind": calling back to mind

definition: not easy to find or get; in short supply

examples.text: Fresh water is scarce on the island during the dry season.
Paper was so scarce that letters were written across old pages.
Parking is scarce near the stadium on game days.

confused.note: Scarce means in short supply; to scare is to frighten.

questions.passage: During the siege, food became so ______ that a single loaf of bread sold for the price of a horse. Families who had once kept full cellars were reduced to boiling leather for soup.
questions.explanation: Bread at the price of a horse shows food was in very short supply.

distractors.why: Uniform means the same throughout, which does not fit.
Cohesive means united, which does not fit.
Discrete means separate, which does not fit.

definition: separate and distinct from other things of the same type

examples.text: Light arrives in discrete packets called photons.
The empire was less a single state than a collection of discrete kingdoms.
The project has four discrete steps, and we are stuck on the first.

confused.note: Discrete means separate; discreet means tactful and careful.

questions.passage: The course is divided into six ______ units. Each has its own textbook, its own teacher, and its own examination, and a student may take them in any order.
questions.explanation: Units with their own books, teachers, and exams are separate and distinct.

distractors.why: Discreet means tactful; it sounds the same but has a different meaning.
Cohesive means closely united, the opposite of separate units.
Reminiscent means bringing to mind, which does not fit.

definition: united and working together well; forming a whole

examples.text: Clay particles form a cohesive mass when wet.
Years of shared hardship made the regiment a cohesive unit.
Our team finally felt cohesive after the weekend tournament.

confused.note: Cohesive means united; coercive means using force.

questions.passage: At the start of the season the team was a collection of talented individuals. By its end the players had become a ______ group, passing without looking and defending as if they shared a single mind.
questions.explanation: Players who move as one have become united.

distractors.why: Discrete means separate, which describes the team at the start.
Lax means careless, which does not fit.
Scarce means in short supply, which does not fit.

definition: to have a relationship in which one thing changes as another does

examples.text: Sales of ice cream correlate with the temperature.
Wealth in the province correlated closely with distance from the river.
My mood correlates strongly with whether I have eaten lunch.

confused.note: To correlate is to vary together; to corroborate is to confirm.

questions.passage: Researchers found that hours of sleep ______ strongly with test scores. On average, each additional hour a student slept was accompanied by a rise of four points.
questions.explanation: Scores rising with hours of sleep shows the two change together.

distractors.why: Imply means to suggest; the sentence describes a measured relationship.
Harbor means to hold or shelter, which does not fit.
Overshadow means to make seem less important, which does not fit.

definition: to be a clear example of an idea or quality; to give it visible form

examples.text: The new constitution embodied the ideals of the revolution.
The old gardener embodies the patience the hero lacks.
My coach embodies the idea that kindness and toughness can go together.

confused.note: To embody is to give form to an idea; to embed is to fix firmly inside something.

questions.passage: For the townspeople, the old lighthouse keeper came to ______ the virtues they most admired. He was punctual, uncomplaining, and had not missed a single night at the lamp in forty years.
questions.explanation: A man who shows a community's ideals in his life gives them visible form.

distractors.why: Recede means to move back, which does not fit.
Capitalize means to take advantage, which does not fit.
Tolerate means to put up with, far weaker than representing an ideal.
